chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that
the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), whenever he sent out a battalion, would supplicate for it.

key_terms.دَعَا لَهَا: Supplicated for it — the act of praying on behalf of another, expressing both spiritual intercession and pastoral leadership
key_terms.سَرِيَّة: A military detachment or expedition sent without the Prophet's personal accompaniment — distinct from ghazwa (a campaign the Prophet led himself). These were typically smaller units dispatched for specific objectives.

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad supplicate for his armies when sending them out?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) had a consistent practice of offering supplication whenever he dispatched a military expedition (sariyya). This hadith reveals the Prophet's deep spiritual care for those under his command, integrating prayer as an essential component of military leadership. The narration, transmitted through the well-known Sakuni chain via Imam al-Sadiq, reflects the Shia understanding that du'a (supplication) is a vital act of leadership and intercession for one's community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that
the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> sent a battallion, supplicated for it’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, dispatched a small group of people for an armed expedition, he would pray in their favor.”
